newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Berlusconi finds spying device in office.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Berlusconi finds spying device in office.

text.p: Former Italian prime minister Silvio Berlusconi said on Friday a tiny bugging device had been found hidden in his office.

Berlusconi, head of the Italian centre-right opposition bloc, told a news conference that the miniaturised radio microphone was discovered on Wednesday in a window recess behind his desk in his central Rome headquarters.
"Experts have told me it was in perfect working condition and capable of transmitting across a range of 300 metres," the media tycoon told reporters, holding up the small microphone.
Italian magistrates have used hi-tech bugging devices in a number of recent anti-corruption probes, including the latest scandal involving alleged graft across a range of state-controlled companies.
Berlusconi is currently standing trial for corruption in Milan concerning alleged kick-backs paid by his media empire in return for lenient audits.
The businessman-turned-politician told Friday's news conference that his lawyers had assured him magistrates were not allowed to use bugging devices against parliamentarians.

"This is a very serious situation, which is even more serious given that we are dealing with the leader of the opposition," Berlusconi said, adding that he had informed judicial authorities about the discovery.

"I want to denounce this as a violation of my person, of my position as a parliamentarian and as leader of Forza Italia," he said. The office where the device was found was used for meetings with his political allies.

Berlusconi swept triumphantly into politics in 1994 at the head of his newly created party Forza Italia and swiftly won a general election. However his government collapsed before the end of the year and he has maintained a low profile following his election defeat in April of this year.
